before: An abstract class may contain abstract methods without bodies. Shape.area() defines a required operation; the concrete Square supplies it.

A Shape reference can refer to a Square. You cannot instantiate Shape itself while it is abstract. Abstract classes can also contain fields, constructors and implemented methods; abstract does not mean every member lacks a body.

Expected output or behavior: 4
. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Add a concrete method to Shape that calls area, then use it through a Shape reference. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: An abstract method names an operation but has no body. Shape declares that its objects need an area method. Square supplies the body, making it a concrete class: a class that can be used to create objects.
An abstract class cannot be created directly with new. Its type can still name a reference to a concrete child object. An abstract class may also have fields, constructors, and methods with bodies.
The program prints 4. This Square's area method is written to return four.
The quiz tries to create Shape directly. Check the class declaration before expecting any output.
